title: Restriction of modules to an open subscheme is exact and preserves injectives; direct image along the open immersion preserves injectives
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme with inclusion $j:U\to X$, and for an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\mathcal G|_U$ be the restricted $\mathcal O_U$-module, $(\mathcal G|_U)(W)=\mathcal G(W)$ for $W\subseteq U$ open [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]; let $j_*:\Mod(\mathcal O_U)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ be the direct image, $(j_*\mathcal H)(W)=\mathcal H(W\cap U)$. Then: (1) the functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_U$, is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]: it is additive and carries a sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules exact at the middle term to one exact at the middle term; (2) if $\mathcal I$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sp-injective-resolutions], then $\mathcal I|_U$ is an injective $\mathcal O_U$-module; (3) if $\mathcal J$ is an injective $\mathcal O_U$-module, then $j_*\mathcal J$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module. Consequently, if $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution of an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, then $\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$ is an injective resolution of $\mathcal F|_U$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$.

proof.text: Restriction is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits by the shared moduleOverFunctor instances of lem-sc-derived-hom-mayer-vietoris, specialized to X.toRingedSpace. Hence it preserves homology and ShortComplex.Exact by Mathlib ShortComplex.Exact.map; no stalk computation is required.

Let P be the direct-sum extension-by-zero presheaf functor. For a monomorphism f of sheaves, f.val is a monomorphism because the forgetful functor preserves finite limits. Each component is injective by PresheafOfModules.injective_of_mono. DirectSum.lmap_injective makes every component of P.map f injective, so PresheafOfModules.mono_of_injective shows P preserves monomorphisms. Sheafification preserves finite limits and therefore monomorphisms; their composite L preserves monomorphisms. Extract L adjoint to restriction from module_extensionByZero_adjunction and apply Adjunction.map_injective. This argument works also for the empty open, using the empty direct sum.

Use Mathlib SheafOfModules.overPushforwardOverAdj for the precise over-site restriction and direct-image functors in the statement. Restriction preserves finite limits by step 1, so Adjunction.preservesInjectiveObjects_of_preservesFiniteLimits gives injectivity of direct images.

For an existing resolution I, construct J with cocomplex the termwise restricted complex. Its terms are injective by step 2. Define the augmentation as singleMapHomologicalComplex.inv.app F followed by the mapped augmentation I.ι. Exact restriction preserves the quasi-isomorphism; the single-complex comparison is an isomorphism, hence the composite is a quasi-isomorphism. The complex equality is reflexivity. The degree-zero augmentation equality simplifies by singleMapHomologicalComplex_inv_app_self. No choice of a resolution and no enough-injectives theorem is needed.
